newsitem.title: EU: EC Report Long-Term Diary for July 14-Dec 31, 1997.
newsitem.headline: EC Report Long-Term Diary for July 14-Dec 31, 1997.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg hosts summit of European Union leaders (December 12-13).
MONDAY, JULY 14
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (1700/1500 GMT) (To July 18). Provisional agenda includes presentation by European Ombudsman of 1996 annual report.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "EU enlargement - The industrial consequences" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is: Commission Directorate-General III (Industry) Head Stefano Micossi. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
TUESDAY, JULY 15

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (0900/0700 GMT) (second of five days). Provisional agenda includes debates on legal protection of biotechnological inventions; rules on voice telephony in a competitive environment; admission of non resident transporters to carry road passengers; international transport of passengers by coach or bus; taxation of lorries used on certain infrastructure; defining a strategy to stregthen air safety.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds weekly meeting. Agenda includes opinions on EU membership applications of East European countries and "Agenda 2000" proposals on the consequences of enlargement for EU policies in areas including budget, agriculture and aid to poorer members.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Union for Europe Group President Jean-Claude Pasty holds press lunch (1300/1100 GMT). Venue: Club de la presse, Allee de la Robertsau. Contact: Union for Europe Group (322) 284 1111.
WEDNESDAY, JULY 16

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (0900/0700 GMT) (third of five days). European Commission presents opinions on EU membership applications of Eastern European countries and "Agenda 2000" proposals on the consequences of enlargement for EU policies in areas including budget, agriculture and aid to poorer members.

Provisional agenda also includes debates on ARIANE book-translation programme; free movement of doctors and mutual recognition of their diplomas; freedom of establishment of national and international "goods/passenger" transporters and mutual recognition of their diplomas; policy and action on the environment and sustainable development; transfer of waste towards non-OECD member states; partnership accords with Moldova, Ukraine.

BRUSSELS - European Congress Consultants and Organisers holds fourth international conference on "Harmonisation of technical requirements for the registration of drugs for human use" (To July 18). Venue: Palais des Exposition, convention centre. Contact: ECCO (322) 647 8780.
THURSDAY, JULY 17
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - French President Jacques Chirac meets European Commission President Santer - followed by a joint n/ conf after lunch (time to be confirmed).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (1000/0900 GMT) (fourth of five days). Agenda includes votes on topical international questions.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - First joint NATO-Russia session.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on official visit (To July 19); meets European Commission President Santer followed by a n/conf at about 1230/1030 GMT or 1300/1100 GMT.
FRIDAY, JULY 18

BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - European Commission and South Africa meet at ministerial level to pursue technical discussions on a future bilateral agreement. (NOTE: This item was previously listed incorrectly as taking place on July 9.)
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin meets European Commission President Santer - followed by a n/conf at about 1230/1030 GMT.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (0900/0700 GMT) (last of five days). Agenda includes votes on extending to Vietnam a cooperation accord between the EU and members of the Association of South East Asian Nations.
MONDAY, JULY 21
- EU institutions closed for Belgian National Day holiday.
TUESDAY, JULY 22
BRUSSELS - EU foreign ministers meet (To July 23). No agenda yet available.
BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To July 23). No agenda yet available.

LUXEMBOURG - The European Finance Convention and the Euro Week hold 11th annual convention (To November 28). Main topics discussed are the euro's impact on financial markets; European payment systems and implications for bank profitability; an overview of the enlargement programme - benefits and disadvantages of the first wave of entries. Speakers include: European Commission President Santer; Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt; European Commissioners Yves-Thibault de Silguy, Mario Monti, Monika Wulf-Mathies, Emma Bonino and Hans van den Broek; European Parliament deputy Karl Von Wogau; Bank of England Governor Eddie George; Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes; Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo de Rato; World Trade Organisation Director General Renato Ruggiero; French Economy Minister Jean Arthuis; European Investment Bank President Brian Unwin.
